stem:
Xavier's school holds a measles vaccination camp. His grandmother asks why healthy children are being vaccinated.

Which statement best explains how vaccination reduces serious infections and their spread?

options.text: Vaccines are medicines taken after someone falls sick, so they cure measles and stop it spreading.
Vaccines prepare the immune system before exposure, so vaccinated children are less likely to become seriously ill and less likely to pass the infection to others.
The first exposure to measles produces the stronger immune response, so vaccination is useful only after a child has already had measles once.
Children in the same class share the same immunity, so vaccinating a few children protects the whole class equally.

teacher.key_rationale: Vaccination prepares immunity before exposure, lowering severe illness and spread. Calling vaccines post-illness cures swaps prevention for treatment. Saying first natural exposure is stronger reverses the vaccination logic. Shared classroom immunity captures a surface group feature.
